title: Motors, Gearboxes and Backlash as a Plant: A Gear Motor Built From Its Data Sheet, and the Gap That an Encoder on the Motor Cannot See

questions.question: Which data sheet numbers are enough to build a brushed motor model?
options: The rotor inertia and the backlash
Voltage, no load speed, stall torque and the gear ratio
The power rating and the weight
questions.explanation: The back voltage constant is the voltage over the no load speed, and the resistance follows from the stall torque. The rest of the model is marked typical.

questions.question: At half the stall torque the output ran at:
questions.explanation: The line from no load speed to stall torque is straight, so half the torque is half the speed.

questions.question: The formula for the time constant gave 0.246 s. The simulated step took:
questions.explanation: The step response reached 63 percent in the time the algebra gave. That agreement is the check on the simulation.

questions.question: After a reversal the output did not move until the gear side had crossed:
options: Nothing: the encoder showed no gap
questions.explanation: On reversing, the gear has to cross the whole gap before it touches the output's other face. Until then the output stays where it was.

questions.question: Why does an encoder on the motor not see backlash?
options: It measures the gear side, and the gap is between that and the output
It only counts in one direction
questions.explanation: The encoder says where the motor's side of the gear is. The output sat a degree either side of the target, depending on which way it had come.

questions.question: Why does a heavy load feel light behind a gearbox?
options: Its inertia is divided by the square of the ratio at the motor
The gearbox carries the load's weight
Friction in the gears holds it
questions.explanation: Through a ratio of n the load turns n times slower, and its inertia seen at the motor is divided by n squared.
